assumptions.condition: The law of \(N\) is invariant under time shifts.
\(G(A)\) contains no directed cycle, with a self-loop counted as a directed cycle of length one.

novel.justification: This contribution-defining restriction describes labeled feed-forward alarm cascades along documented access, aggregation, and core-network dependencies, where propagation is modeled over a window short enough that slower remediation feedback is external to the Hawkes mechanism. Because self-loops are admissible in \(G(A)\) before the restriction is imposed, acyclicity itself forces \(A_{ii}=0\).

This identification-specific exclusion is necessary because \(A=0\) yields independent homogeneous Poisson coordinates whose observable law is unchanged for every \(\beta>0\), as characterized separately in \(\text{prop:empty-graph-equivalence}\). It is appropriate for scientific windows selected to contain at least one reproducible cross-label excitation channel.

definitions.name: Acyclic common-decay closure class
definitions.construction: \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:p\geq2,\ \Delta>0,\ N\text{ is stationary with the stated exponential Hawkes intensity},\ \mu_i>0,\ \beta>0,\ A_{ij}\geq0,\ G(A)\text{ contains no directed cycle under the convention that a self-loop is a cycle of length one, for every }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\}\).

definitions.name: Nonempty acyclic common-decay class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}\text{ satisfies every member property of }\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\text{ and }A\neq0\text{ for every }p\geq2\text{ and }\Delta>0\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed conditioning-margin class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}\text{ satisfies every member property of }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+},\ \sigma_r(\Gamma_1)\geq\kappa,\ e^{-\beta\Delta}\in[\kappa,1-\kappa],\ \beta+\lVert\mu\rVert_2+\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa^{-1},\ \min_i\lambda_i\geq\kappa,\ \lambda_{\min}\{\Omega(\theta)\}\geq\kappa,\ \min_{i\neq j:Z_{ij}\neq0}|Z_{ij}|\geq\kappa\text{ for every }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\ p\geq2,\text{ and }\Delta>0\}\).

definitions.name: Nuisance-regular acyclic closure class
definitions.construction: \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}\text{ satisfies every member property of }\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}},\ e^{-\beta\Delta}\in[\kappa_0,1-\kappa_0],\ \beta+\lVert\mu\rVert_2+\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0^{-1},\ \min_{1\leq i\leq p}\lambda_i\geq\kappa_0,\ \lambda_{\min}\{\Omega(\theta)\}\geq\kappa_0\text{ for every }p\geq2\text{ and }\Delta>0\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed-bin mean and lag covariances
definitions.construction: \(X_k=N(((k+1)\Delta))-N(k\Delta),\quad m=\mathbb E[X_0],\quad\Gamma_k=\mathbb E[(X_k-m)(X_0-m)^{\mathsf T}]\) for every \(k\geq0\).

definitions.name: Basis-invariant two-lag inverse
definitions.construction: For \(r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)>0\), choose any orthonormal \(O\) spanning \(S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\), set \(R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1\), \(F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\), \(q=\operatorname{tr}(F)/r\), \(\beta^\star=-\Delta^{-1}\log q\), \(E=q^{-1}F-I_r\), \(L^\star=-\beta^\star I_r+\Delta^{-1}\sum_{h=1}^{r-1}(-1)^{h+1}E^h/h\), \(H^\star=L^\star(F-I_r)^{-1}\), \(K^\star=O(H^\star)^2R\), \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\), \(\lambda^\star=m/\Delta\), \(A_{ii}^\star=0\), \(A_{ij}^\star=\max\{Z_{ij}^\star,0\}/\lambda_j^\star\) for \(i\neq j\), and \(\mu^\star=(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star)\lambda^\star\); define \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta^\star,A^\star,\mu^\star)\).

definitions.name: Covariance-only inverse
definitions.construction: Apply the transition and logarithm steps of \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\) to \((\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), form \(\widetilde C_{+}(t)=Oe^{L^\star t}(H^\star)^2R\), set \(D^\star=\Delta^{-1}[\Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)\{\widetilde C_{+}(t)+\widetilde C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt]\), set \(\lambda^\star=\operatorname{diag}(D^\star)\), and complete the edge and baseline steps of \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\); the output is \(\Psi_{\Delta,r}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\).

definitions.name: Raw-moment centering map
definitions.construction: For \(\xi=(m,\operatorname{vec}(M_1),\operatorname{vec}(M_2))\), set \(\mathcal C(\xi)=(m,M_1-mm^{\mathsf T},M_2-mm^{\mathsf T})=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=\eta\).

definitions.name: Rank-adaptive moment inverse
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat\xi_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k\), \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)=(\widehat m_n,\widehat\Gamma_{1,n},\widehat\Gamma_{2,n})\), and \(\widehat r_n=\sum_{s=1}^p\mathbf1\{\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>t_n\}\). Use a fixed Borel-measurable singular-value-decomposition rule to choose the truncated left singular subspace and its orthonormal basis. For \(\widehat r_n>0\), compute every starred intermediate in \(\text{def:two-lag-inverse}\), and let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the event that \(\sigma_{\widehat r_n}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>\sigma_{\widehat r_n+1}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})\), with \(\sigma_{p+1}=0\), the resulting \(q\) lies in \((0,1)\), every inverse in that definition exists, every component of \(\lambda^\star=\widehat m_n/\Delta\) used as a divisor is positive, and \(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star\) is invertible; declare \(\mathcal V_n\) false when \(\widehat r_n=0\). Set \(\widehat\theta_n=\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\) on \(\mathcal V_n\), and set the measurable sentinel \(\widehat\theta_n=(1,0,\mathbf1_p)\) on \(\mathcal V_n^c\). When \(\widehat r_n=0\), report the empty graph and leave \(\beta\) set-valued over \((0,\infty)\); when \(\widehat r_n>0\) but \(\mathcal V_n\) fails, report abstention. The sentinel is used only to make every numerical random object total.

definitions.name: Lag-window and composite plug-in covariance estimators
definitions.construction: For the Bartlett kernel \(w(x)=(1-|x|)_+\), set \(\overline Y_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k=\widehat\xi_n\) and \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Xi_0+\sum_{h=1}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)(\widehat\Xi_h+\widehat\Xi_h^{\mathsf T})\), where \(\widehat\Xi_h=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-h-3}(Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\), with an empty inner sum interpreted as zero. This Bartlett matrix is positive semidefinite for every sample. On \(\mathcal V_n\), define \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), evaluating the derivative through the smooth representative \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\) before positive parts, and set \(\widehat W_n=0\) on \(\mathcal V_n^c\). Define the measurable event \(\mathcal D_n=\mathcal V_n\cap\{Z_{ij}^\star\neq0\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\}\). On \(\mathcal D_n\), define \(\widehat V_n=D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\); on \(\mathcal D_n^c\), set \(\widehat V_n=0\) as a numerical placeholder. The optional \(\widehat V_n\) is not used to define \(\widehat W_n\) or any graph interval.

definitions.name: Fixed-margin graph and parameter confidence sets
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal V_n\), let \(\widehat z\) be the vector of upper-triangular entries of the recovered signed jump \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\); on \(\mathcal V_n^c\), set \(\widehat z=0\). With the sentinel in \(\text{def:rank-adaptive-estimator}\), this gives the total identity \(\widehat z=\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)\). Let \(\widehat W_n\) be the total positive-semidefinite signed-score covariance in \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\). Conditional on \(\widehat W_n\), for \(\mathcal Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat W_n)\), including singular \(\widehat W_n\), define \(c_{n,1-\alpha}=\inf\{x\in[0,\infty):P(\max_{i<j}|\mathcal Z_{ij}|\leq x\mid\widehat W_n)\geq1-\alpha\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). On \(\mathcal V_n\), set \(I_{ij,n}=[\widehat z_{ij}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n,\widehat z_{ij}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n]\), and let \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) be the set of labeled acyclic graphs which, for every \(i<j\), use no edge only if \(0\in I_{ij,n}\), use \(j\to i\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(0,\infty)\neq\varnothing\), and use \(i\to j\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(-\infty,0)\neq\varnothing\). On \(\mathcal V_n^c\), set every \(I_{ij,n}=\mathbb R\) and let \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) be the set of all labeled acyclic graphs. Define \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\) as the full-parameter Wald ellipsoid only on \(\mathcal D_n\) when \(\widehat V_n\) makes that ellipsoid well defined; on every other sample set \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)=\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}\). This optional parameter benchmark is not used in signed-edge or graph coverage.

definitions.name: Parameter and binned-law topologies
definitions.construction: Set \(\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}=\{(\beta,A,\mu):P_{\beta,A,\mu}\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\}\) and \(\Theta_{\Delta,p}^{+}=\{\theta\in\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}:A\neq0\}\). Equip \(\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}\) with \(\rho_{\Theta}(\theta,\theta')=1\wedge\{|\beta-\beta'|+\lVert A-A'\rVert_{\mathrm F}+\lVert\mu-\mu'\rVert_2\}\), and equip the induced binned laws with \(\rho_{\mathrm{law}}(P,P')=\sum_{h=1}^{\infty}2^{-h}\{1\wedge\lVert P_{(X_0,\ldots,X_{h-1})}-P'_{(X_0,\ldots,X_{h-1})}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\).

definitions.name: One-lag observable, fiber, and three-node support strata
definitions.construction: For \(\theta\in\Theta_{\Delta,p}^{+}\), set \(\mathcal O_1(\theta)=(m(\theta),\Gamma_1(\theta))\) and \(\mathfrak F_1(o)=\{\theta'\in\Theta_{\Delta,p}^{+}:\mathcal O_1(\theta')=o\}\). Let \(\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\) contain every labeling of the three-node chain, fork, and diamond motifs. For \(G_0\in\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\), set \(\Theta_{s,G_0}=\{\theta\in\Theta_{\Delta,3}^{+}:G(A)=G_0,\ \operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1(\theta))=s\}\). A subset \(U\subseteq\Theta_{s,G_0}\) is relatively open exactly when \(U=V\cap\Theta_{s,G_0}\) for some \(\rho_{\Theta}\)-open \(V\subseteq\Theta_{\Delta,3}^{+}\).

definitions.name: One-lag compatibility-fiber handle
definitions.construction: For each \(G_0\in\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\), eliminate \((\beta,A,\mu)\) from the polynomial-exponential equations defining \(\mathfrak F_1\{\mathcal O_1(\theta)\}\); apply real-algebraic stratification within each \(\Theta_{s,G_0}\), enforce Hawkes positivity, and compare distinct surviving parameters in \(\rho_{\mathrm{law}}\).

definitions.name: Boundary separation and adaptation frontier
definitions.construction: For \(r(\theta)=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1(\theta))\), set \(\delta(\theta)=0\) when \(A=0\), and otherwise set \(\delta(\theta)=1\wedge\sigma_{r(\theta)}(\Gamma_1(\theta))\wedge\min_{i\neq j:Z_{ij}(\theta)\neq0}|Z_{ij}(\theta)|\). Inside \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), let \(\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta)=\{P_{\theta}\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0):\delta(\theta)\geq\delta\}\). For \(\mathfrak U_n=(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal T_n)\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)\), define \(R_{G,n,\kappa_0}(\delta)=\inf_{\mathfrak U_n\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)}\sup_{P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta)}\mathbb E_{\theta}[\ell_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathcal G_n,G(A))]\) and \(R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(\delta)=\inf_{\mathfrak U_n\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)}\sup_{P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta)}\mathbb E_{\theta}[\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)]\); the focal frontier is \(\mathfrak R_{n,\kappa_0}(\delta)=(R_{G,n,\kappa_0}(\delta),R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(\delta))\).

definitions.name: Rank-boundary confidence-union handle
definitions.construction: Within \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), construct contiguous local experiments for the raw-moment process \(Y\) along sequences indexed by \(\delta_n=\delta(\theta_n)\), while keeping the decay, parameter-envelope, intensity, long-run-variance, derived mixing, derived moment, and bandwidth conditions regular. Derive matching lower and upper bounds for \(\mathfrak R_{n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n)\) under \(\ell_{\mathrm{inc}}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}\), and invert rank-indexed signed-score tests without first selecting one rank.

definitions.name: Stable common-exponential Hawkes class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}=\{P_{N,\mu,\beta,A}:p\geq2,\ \Delta>0,\ N\text{ is stationary with the stated common-exponential Hawkes intensity},\ \mu_i>0,\ \beta>0,\ A_{ij}\geq0\text{ for every }i,j\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\ \rho(A/\beta)<1\}\), where \(\rho\) denotes spectral radius. No acyclicity, zero-diagonal, orientation, or full-rank condition is part of this class definition.

definitions.name: Full-rank stable no-alias population moment image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\) be the population moment image
\[
 \left\{(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 \det(A)\neq0,\quad
 \operatorname{spec}\{\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\}\subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population moments}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
This is an image-defined domain, not an additional observable assumption.

definitions.name: Domain-restricted full-rank stable two-lag inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\), set
\[
 \lambda^\dagger=m/\Delta,\quad D^\dagger=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^\dagger),\quad
 T^\dagger=\Gamma_2\Gamma_1^{-1},\quad
 B^\dagger=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(T^\dagger),
\]
\[
 J^\dagger=(B^\dagger)^{-1}(T^\dagger-I_p),\quad
 K^\dagger=(J^\dagger)^{-2}\Gamma_1,\quad
 Q^\dagger=\int_0^\infty e^{B^\dagger u}D^\dagger e^{(B^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}u}\,du,
\]
and
\[
 s^\dagger=p^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\!\left\{K^\dagger(Q^\dagger)^{-1}+(B^\dagger)^2\right\},\quad
 \beta^\dagger=(s^\dagger)^{1/2},\quad
 A^\dagger=B^\dagger+\beta^\dagger I_p,\quad
 \mu^\dagger=(I_p-A^\dagger/\beta^\dagger)\lambda^\dagger,
\]
where the square root is the positive real square root. Define the domain-restricted map
\[
 \Phi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\Delta,p}:\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\longrightarrow
 \mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R^{p\times p}\times\mathbb R^p,
 \qquad
 \Phi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\Delta,p}(\eta)=(\beta^\dagger,A^\dagger,\mu^\dagger).
\]

definitions.name: Positive-rank zero-diagonal restricted-no-alias population moment image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\) be the population moment image
\[
 \left\{(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 A\neq0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(A)=0,\\
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\left.\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\right|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\right)
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population moments}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
The restriction is well defined because \(\operatorname{im}(A)\) is invariant under \(A-\beta I_p\).  This is an image-defined domain; it does not require \(A\) to be invertible, acyclic, or free of reciprocal pairs, and it does not encode a recovered parameter as an observable premise.

definitions.name: Domain-restricted singular-feedback two-lag inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\), set
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),\quad S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),
\]
choose any \(O\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\) with \(O^{\mathsf T}O=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{im}(O)=S\), and define
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1,\quad
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1},
\]
\[
 \lambda^\sharp=m/\Delta,\quad D^\sharp=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^\sharp),
 \quad L^\sharp=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F),
\]
\[
 \beta^\sharp=-\operatorname{tr}(L^\sharp)/r,\quad
 A_S^\sharp=L^\sharp+\beta^\sharp I_r,\quad
 H^\sharp=L^\sharp(F-I_r)^{-1},
\]
\[
 K^\sharp=O(H^\sharp)^2R,\quad
 Z^\sharp=K^\sharp-(K^\sharp)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 P^\sharp=OO^{\mathsf T},\quad
 W^\sharp=O^{\mathsf T}(D^\sharp)^{-1}O,
\]
\[
 \mathsf C^\sharp=
 \{OA_S^\sharp-Z^\sharp(I_p-P^\sharp)(D^\sharp)^{-1}O\}
 (W^\sharp)^{-1}O^{\mathsf T}+Z^\sharp(I_p-P^\sharp),
\]
and
\[
 A^\sharp=\mathsf C^\sharp(D^\sharp)^{-1},\quad
 \mu^\sharp=(I_p-A^\sharp/\beta^\sharp)\lambda^\sharp.
\]
Define the domain-restricted map
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}:\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}
 \longrightarrow\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R^{p\times p}\times\mathbb R^p,
 \quad
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}(\eta)
 =(\beta^\sharp,A^\sharp,\mu^\sharp).
\]

definitions.name: Full-rank stable covariance-only population image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\) be the population covariance image
\[
 \left\{(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 \det(A)\neq0,\quad
 \operatorname{spec}\{\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\}
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population covariances}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
This is a population image under \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), not a collection defined by observable gate conditions.

definitions.name: Domain-restricted full-rank covariance-only inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\), set
\[
 T^0=\Gamma_2\Gamma_1^{-1},\qquad
 B^0=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(T^0),\qquad
 J^0=(B^0)^{-1}(T^0-I_p),\qquad
 K^0=(J^0)^{-2}\Gamma_1,
\]
\[
 \widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{fr}}(t)=e^{B^0t}K^0,\qquad
 D^0=\Delta^{-1}\!\left[
 \Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{\widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{fr}}(t)
   +\widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{fr}}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt\right],
\]
and
\[
 \lambda^0=\operatorname{diag}(D^0),\qquad m^0=\Delta\lambda^0.
\]
Define the domain-restricted covariance-only map by
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr},0}(\gamma)
 =\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}(m^0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2).
\]

definitions.name: Restricted-rank stable covariance-only population image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\) be the population covariance image
\[
 \left\{(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 A\neq0,\quad \operatorname{diag}(A)=0,\\
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(
 \left.\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\right|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\right)
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population covariances}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
This is a population image under \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), not a collection defined by observable gate conditions.  It permits singular excitation, directed cycles, reciprocal pairs, and isolated labels.

definitions.name: Domain-restricted singular-feedback covariance-only inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in
\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\), set
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),\qquad S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),
\]
choose any \(O\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\) with \(O^{\mathsf T}O=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{im}(O)=S\), and set
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1,\qquad
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1},
\]
\[
 L^\sharp=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F),\qquad
 H^\sharp=L^\sharp(F-I_r)^{-1},\qquad
 \widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{rs}}(t)
 =Oe^{L^\sharp t}(H^\sharp)^2R,
\]
\[
 D^0=\Delta^{-1}\!\left[
 \Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{\widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{rs}}(t)
  +\widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{rs}}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt\right],
 \qquad \lambda^0=\operatorname{diag}(D^0),
 \qquad m^0=\Delta\lambda^0.
\]
Define
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs},0}(\gamma)
 =\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}(m^0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2).
\]

definitions.name: Isolated invertible-block stable population moment image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\) be the population moment image
\[
 \left\{(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exist }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\text{ and a set }I\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,p\},\\
 1\leq r=|I|\leq p-1,\quad E_I=(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_r})\text{ for }i_1<\cdots<i_r\text{ the elements of }I,\\
 A=E_IA_IE_I^{\mathsf T},\quad A_I\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},\quad A_I\geq0,\quad \det(A_I)\neq0,\quad \rho(A_I)<\beta,\\
 \operatorname{spec}\{\Delta(A_I-\beta I_r)\}\subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population moments}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
The inequalities \(A_I\geq0\) are entrywise.  Labels outside \(I\) retain their strictly positive baseline intensities but have no incoming or outgoing excitation.  This is an image-defined domain: no claim is made that membership in it can be certified from an arbitrary observed triple beyond the recovery statements proved on the image.

definitions.name: Isolated invertible-block two-lag inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\), set
\[
 S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),\qquad
 I^\circ=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:e_i\in S\},\qquad
 r^\circ=|I^\circ|,
\]
and let \(E^\circ=E_{I^\circ}\) be the ordered coordinate selector.  With \(\Gamma_1^\dagger\) denoting the Moore--Penrose inverse, define
\[
 F^\circ=(E^\circ)^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2\Gamma_1^\dagger E^\circ,\qquad
 L^\circ=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F^\circ),\qquad
 J^\circ=\int_0^\Delta e^{L^\circ u}\,du,
\]
\[
 G_1^\circ=(E^\circ)^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1E^\circ,\qquad
 K^\circ=(J^\circ)^{-2}G_1^\circ,\qquad
 \lambda^\circ=m/\Delta,\qquad
 D_I^\circ=(E^\circ)^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^\circ)E^\circ,
\]
\[
 Q^\circ=\int_0^\infty e^{L^\circ u}D_I^\circ e^{(L^\circ)^{\mathsf T}u}\,du,\qquad
 s^\circ=(r^\circ)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\{K^\circ(Q^\circ)^{-1}+(L^\circ)^2\},
\]
\[
 \beta^\circ=(s^\circ)^{1/2},\qquad
 A^\circ=E^\circ(L^\circ+\beta^\circ I_{r^\circ})(E^\circ)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 \mu^\circ=(I_p-A^\circ/\beta^\circ)\lambda^\circ.
\]
Here \((J^\circ)^{-2}=(J^\circ)^{-1}(J^\circ)^{-1}\), as required by the positive-lag identity \(\Gamma_1=J^2K\).  Define
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}:\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}
 \longrightarrow\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R^{p\times p}\times\mathbb R^p,
 \qquad
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}(\eta)=(\beta^\circ,A^\circ,\mu^\circ).
\]

definitions.name: Isolated invertible-block stable covariance population image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\) be the population covariance image
\[
 \left\{(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exist }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\text{ and a set }I\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,p\},\\
 1\leq r=|I|\leq p-1,\quad E_I=(e_{i_1},\ldots,e_{i_r})\text{ for }i_1<\cdots<i_r\text{ the elements of }I,\\
 A=E_IA_IE_I^{\mathsf T},\quad A_I\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},\quad A_I\geq0,\quad \det(A_I)\neq0,\quad \rho(A_I)<\beta,\\
 \operatorname{spec}\{\Delta(A_I-\beta I_r)\}\subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population covariances}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
The inequalities \(A_I\geq0\) are entrywise.  This is a population image under \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), not an observable gate imposed on arbitrary covariance triples.

definitions.name: Isolated invertible-block covariance-only inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\), set
\[
 S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),\qquad
 I^0=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:e_i\in S\},\qquad
 r^0=|I^0|,
\]
and let \(E^0=E_{I^0}\) be the ordered coordinate selector.  Define
\[
 F^0=(E^0)^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2\Gamma_1^\dagger E^0,\qquad
 L^0=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F^0),\qquad
 J^0=\int_0^\Delta e^{L^0u}\,du,
\]
\[
 G_1^0=(E^0)^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1E^0,\qquad
 K^0=(J^0)^{-2}G_1^0,\qquad
 \widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{ib}}(t)=E^0e^{L^0t}K^0(E^0)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 D^0=\Delta^{-1}\!\left[\Gamma_0-
 \int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{\widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{ib}}(t)+\widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{ib}}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt\right],
 \qquad \lambda^0=\operatorname{diag}(D^0),
 \qquad m^0=\Delta\lambda^0.
\]
Define
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib},0}(\gamma)
 =\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}(m^0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2).
\]

definitions.name: Complete Hawkes conditional response in future-row orientation
definitions.construction:
For a law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\), define its complete nonsingular conditional-response matrix by
\[
 g(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 C_{+}(t)D^{-1},&t>0,\\
 C_{+}(-t)^{\mathsf T}D^{-1},&t<0,\\
 0,&t=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
The value at zero is immaterial for convolution and integration.  The normalization is on the right because \(C_{+}(t)_{ij}=\operatorname{Cov}(dN_i(t),dN_j(0))/dt^2=g^{ij}(t)\lambda_j\).

definitions.name: Stable nonzero restricted-strip population moment image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\) be the population moment image
\[
 \left\{(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 A\neq0,\qquad
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\left.\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\right|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\right)
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population moments}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
This image definition imposes no full-rank, zero-diagonal, coordinate-support, isolated-label, acyclicity, or invertible-active-block restriction.

definitions.name: Stable nonzero restricted-strip covariance population image
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\) be the population covariance image
\[
 \left\{(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2):\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists }(\beta,A,\mu)\text{ inducing a law in }\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}},\\
 A\neq0,\qquad
 \operatorname{spec}\!\left(\left.\Delta(A-\beta I_p)\right|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\right)
 \subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\},\\
 \text{and }\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\text{ are that law's population covariances}
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
This is the covariance-only image of exactly the same nonempty stable restricted-strip regime as \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\).

definitions.name: Broad stable two-lag Wiener--Hopf inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), set
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),\qquad S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),
\]
choose any \(O\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\) with \(O^{\mathsf T}O=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{im}(O)=S\), and define
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1,\quad
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1},
\]
\[
 L^{\mathrm{WH}}=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F),\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=L^{\mathrm{WH}}(F-I_r)^{-1},\quad
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=O(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R,
\]
and, for \(t>0\),
\[
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=Oe^{L^{\mathrm{WH}}t}(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R.
\]
Set \(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}=m/\Delta\), \(D^{\mathrm{WH}}=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}})\), and
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)(D^{\mathrm{WH}})^{-1},&t>0,\\
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(-t)^{\mathsf T}(D^{\mathrm{WH}})^{-1},&t<0,\\
 0,&t=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Let \(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}\) be the unique matrix function whose entries are causal and in \(L^1(\mathbb R_+)\) and which satisfies
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)
 +(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}*g^{\mathrm{WH}})(t),\qquad t>0,
\]
where
\[
 (\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}*g^{\mathrm{WH}})(t)
 =\int_0^\infty\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(s)g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t-s)\,ds
\]
uses ordinary matrix multiplication inside the integral.  Finally set
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)\,dt,\quad
 M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty t\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)\,dt,
\]
\[
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}\mathbf 1_p,\quad
 u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}\mathbf 1_p,
\]
\[
 \beta^{\mathrm{WH}}=u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}/u_1^{\mathrm{WH}},\qquad
 A^{\mathrm{WH}}=\beta^{\mathrm{WH}}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}},\qquad
 \mu^{\mathrm{WH}}=(I_p-M_0^{\mathrm{WH}})\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 =(\beta^{\mathrm{WH}},A^{\mathrm{WH}},\mu^{\mathrm{WH}}).
\]

definitions.name: Broad stable covariance-only Wiener--Hopf inverse
definitions.construction:
For \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), perform the \(r,S,O,R,F,L^{\mathrm{WH}},H^{\mathrm{WH}},K^{\mathrm{WH}}\), and \(C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}\) steps in \(\text{def:wiener-hopf-two-lag-inverse}\) using \((\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\).  Set
\[
 D^{\mathrm{WH},0}=\Delta^{-1}\!\left[
 \Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)+C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt
 \right],
\]
\[
 \lambda^{\mathrm{WH},0}=\operatorname{diag}(D^{\mathrm{WH},0}),
 \qquad m^{\mathrm{WH},0}=\Delta\lambda^{\mathrm{WH},0},
\]
and define
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH},0}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 =\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m^{\mathrm{WH},0},\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2).
\]

statements.statement: For every law in \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\), \(Q\succ0\), \(C_{+}(t)=e^{Bt}K\) for \(t>0\), \(K=A(2\beta I_p-A)Q\), \(K-K^{\mathsf T}=AD-DA^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Gamma_k=T^{k-1}J^2K\) for every \(k\geq1\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(K)=\operatorname{im}(A)\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\), including singular, disconnected, repeated-pole, diamond, and proportional-row cases.
statements.justification: This identity is the algebraic compression that turns a full covariance function into an observable finite-dimensional semigroup without assuming \(A\) invertible.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 derives the continuous Wiener--Hopf relation, while EtesamiZhangSinghalKiyavash2016 Section 4, Equations (13)--(16), works with the full lag-indexed covariance transform; neither states this exact fixed-bin factorization or the image equality for singular acyclic \(A\).
statements.consumer: The image equality supplies the observable state space on which the two-lag recovery theorem is defined.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), the map \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\) is well defined and basis invariant, \(r\geq1\), \(F\) represents \(T|_S\), \(q=e^{-\beta\Delta}\), \(E^r=0\), and \(\Phi_{\Delta,r}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu)\). In particular, \((m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\) identifies the labeled graph and every amplitude, decay, and baseline exactly even when \(A\) is singular, disconnected, or has repeated poles.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates a finite sufficient statistic and an explicit inverse for a causal network observed only through coarse counts.
statements.gap: Koyama2025 Section 3.4, page 8, Theorem 2 and Equation (18), proves \(F_{\Delta t}^{(cg)}(\nu\Delta t)=F^{(hw)}(\nu)\Delta t+O(\Delta t^3)\) as \(\Delta t\to0\), and Corollary 1 compares that surrogate spectrum with the binned spectrum; Section 3.5, pages 8--9, Equations (19)--(20), defines a quadratic-form estimator. Kirchner2016 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Equation (21), proves \(N^{(\Delta)}\Rightarrow N\) only as \(\Delta\to0\), while Section 3.3, Equations (25)--(28), gives parallel INAR(\(\infty\)) and Hawkes lag equations. EtesamiZhangSinghalKiyavash2016 Corollary 4 and Proposition 6 require full spectral zeros and Laplace transforms, and ZhouPapadogeorgou2025 Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.1 use the full aggregated-count law; none gives an exact finite-\(\Delta\) inverse for the original labeled process from one mean and two covariance matrices.
statements.consumer: QiaoCaiWuXiangZhangHao2023's metropolitan cellular-alarm setting can recover within-bin direction at its native one-to-nine-second resolution without imputing latent event times.

statements.statement: Within \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\), \(\Gamma_1=0\) if and only if \(A=0\). On this stratum \(N_1,\ldots,N_p\) are independent homogeneous Poisson processes with rates \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_p\), every \(\beta>0\) induces the same observable law, and \(\beta\) is not identified.
statements.justification: The proposition states the exact boundary on which decay recovery must fail and prevents an estimator from fabricating information at the empty graph.
statements.gap: The finite-bin papers treat positive-excitation parameterizations or likelihood identifiability and do not state this complete two-lag observational-equivalence class.
statements.consumer: The proposition tells a graph-recovery pipeline when it must report a set-valued decay rather than a numerical estimate.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), \(\Psi_{\Delta,r}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu)\). Equivalently, after the positive-lag inverse reconstructs \(\widetilde C_{+}(t)=C_{+}(t)\) on \((0,\Delta]\), the formula \(D=\Delta^{-1}[\Gamma_0-\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)\{C_{+}(t)+C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt]\) recovers \(\lambda=\operatorname{diag}(D)\), so the mean is redundant.
statements.justification: The result determines whether the diagonal jump in zero-lag bin covariance carries all missing first-order information.
statements.gap: Hawkes1971Spectra and BacryMuzy2016 keep intensity as a separate first-order input, while AchabBacryGaiffasMastromatteoMuzy2017 adds third-order cumulants rather than isolating intensity from \(\Gamma_0\).
statements.consumer: Legacy alarm archives that retain covariance summaries but not reliable marginal count totals can still identify the directed Hawkes mechanism.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), the bin-count sequence \(X\) is strongly mixing at a geometric rate. Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). Uniformly over \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), the Poisson immigration--birth representation has genealogical depth at most \(p-1\): every child follows a directed edge of \(G(A)\), so a longer lineage would repeat a label and create a directed cycle. Conditional offspring delays have density \(\beta e^{-\beta u}\), \(\beta\geq\underline\beta=-\Delta^{-1}\log(1-\kappa)\), every event has total offspring mean at most \(\overline\nu=\overline a/\underline\beta\), and the total immigrant rate is at most \(\overline\mu\). Consequently the cluster duration has the uniform tail bound \(P_{\theta}(D_{\mathrm{cl}}>u)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}u}\), where \(c_{\mathrm{mix}}=\underline\beta/2\) and \(C_{\mathrm{mix}}=1+\{1+2\overline\mu c_{\mathrm{mix}}^{-1}e^{c_{\mathrm{mix}}\Delta}\}\sum_{d=1}^{p-1}(2\overline a/\underline\beta)^d\). Coupling the restrictions of the immigrant Poisson measure on the two sides of a bin gap then gives \(\alpha_{X,\theta}(h)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}h\Delta}\) for every integer \(h\geq1\), and \(\alpha_{Y,\theta}(h)\leq C_{\mathrm{mix}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{mix}}(h-2)_{+}\Delta}\) for every integer \(h\geq1\).
statements.justification: This lemma turns feed-forward structure and bounded primitive parameters into the uniform dependence rate required by the HAC argument.
statements.gap: BolyCheyssonNguyen2024 provides compatible general multivariate Hawkes mixing background but does not state this geometric rate from finite genealogical depth; the rate and constants here come from the acyclic common-exponential cluster construction.
statements.consumer: The raw-moment central limit theorem can invoke a derived uniform geometric rate instead of assuming one as a separate model restriction.

statements.statement: Every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\) has finite bin-count moments of every order. Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). Uniformly over \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), the total progeny of any immigrant cluster is dominated by a depth-\(p-1\) Poisson branching tree whose moment-generating functions obey \(g_0(z)=e^z\) and \(g_d(z)=\exp[z+\overline\nu\{g_{d-1}(z)-1\}]\). For every integer \(u\in\{1,\ldots,16\}\), differentiating the stationary Poisson-cluster generating functional and using the duration bound in \(\text{lem:finite-depth-geometric-mixing}\) gives \[\operatorname{cum}_u(\lVert X_0\rVert_1)\leq\overline\mu\left[\Delta g_{p-1}^{(u)}(0)+2c_{\mathrm{mix}}^{-1}\{C_{\mathrm{mix}}g_{p-1}^{(2u)}(0)\}^{1/2}\right].\] The complete moment--cumulant formulas through order sixteen therefore yield the named finite constant \(M_8=M_8(p,\Delta,\kappa)\), the bound \(\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}\mathbb E_{\theta}\lVert X_0\rVert_2^8\leq M_8\), and \(\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}\mathbb E_{\theta}\lVert X_0\rVert_2^{16}<\infty\).
statements.justification: The recursive cluster bound supplies eighth moments of the quadratic raw-moment process needed for explicit four-point cumulant summability and uniform long-run covariance estimation.
statements.gap: CheyssonLang2022 assumes moment regularity for its spectral limit theory; it does not derive a uniform sixteenth-bin-count envelope from bounded acyclic Hawkes primitives.
statements.consumer: Uniform HAC consistency and Gaussian calibration no longer depend on an unexplained independent moment assumption.

statements.statement: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), \(\widehat\xi_n\to\xi\) and \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)\to\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\) in probability. Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). The derived geometric-mixing and sixteenth-bin-count bounds imply that \(\Omega(\theta)\) is finite uniformly over \(P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\) and \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\{\sqrt n(\widehat\xi_n-\xi(\theta))\},\mathcal N\{0,\Omega(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0.\] Because \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)\) and \(\eta=\mathcal C(\xi)=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), the same uniform statement holds for \(\sqrt n(\widehat\eta_n-\eta(\theta))\) with covariance \(D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}\Omega(\theta)D\mathcal C_{\xi(\theta)}^{\mathsf T}\). If \(b_n\to\infty\) and \(b_n=o(n^{1/2})\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: A joint dependent-data limit for precisely the moments entering the inverse is required before any graph-wide uncertainty statement is credible.
statements.gap: CheyssonLang2022 proves fixed-bin Whittle asymptotics, while BolyCheyssonNguyen2024 supplies general mixing background; neither derives the finite-depth uniform envelopes or the joint raw-lag-moment Gaussian and HAC limits in the coordinates of this inverse.
statements.consumer: The rank-adaptive inverse and simultaneous graph confidence set use this Gaussian moment experiment.

statements.statement: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), if \(t_n\downarrow0\), \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\), \(a_n\downarrow0\), and \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), then \(\mathbb P(\widehat r_n=r)\to1\), \(\widehat\theta_n\to(\beta,A,\mu)\) in probability, and \(\mathbb P(\widehat G_n=G(A))\to1\). Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). On \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), under the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions, rank selection is uniformly consistent and the structural estimator is uniformly root-\(n\) tight: \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}(\widehat r_n\neq r(\theta))\longrightarrow0,\] \[\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\!\left[\sqrt n\{ |\widehat\beta_n-\beta|+\lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\mathrm F}+\lVert\widehat\mu_n-\mu\rVert_2\}>M\right]=0.\] For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: The theorem converts exact identification into a rank-adaptive estimator while making every conditioning margin explicit.
statements.gap: CheyssonLang2022 differentiates a smooth Whittle criterion, KoltchinskiiLounici2016Projectors treats basis-free spectral projectors under independent Gaussian sampling, and existing Hawkes graph estimators do not differentiate a restricted logarithm after random image selection.
statements.consumer: The result gives consistent de-aliased weights and support for the low-resolution cellular-alarm network studied by QiaoCaiWuXiangZhangHao2023.

statements.statement: Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). If \(t_n,a_n\downarrow0\), \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\), and \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), then the separately thresholded graph \(\widehat G_n=\{j\to i:\widehat A_{ij}>a_n\}\) satisfies \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\widehat G_n\neq G(A)\}\longrightarrow0.\]
statements.justification: Vanishing thresholds separate model selection from fixed-level confidence inversion and eliminate persistent false inclusions at null coordinates.
statements.gap: Fixed-level simultaneous intervals control graph inclusion but cannot make null-coordinate selection errors vanish; existing exact-event-time Hawkes selectors do not establish this uniform fixed-bin inverse result.
statements.consumer: Cellular-alarm analysts obtain a support-consistent point graph separately from the conservative graph confidence set.

statements.statement: For fixed \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\), the composite \(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C\), evaluated through the signed jump before the positive-part edge map, is Fr\'{e}chet differentiable at \(\xi(\theta)\). Let \[W(\theta)=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\,\Omega(\theta)\,D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}^{\mathsf T}.\] Under the derived geometric-mixing and eighth-moment lemmas and the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions of \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\left[\sqrt n\left\{\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)-\zeta(\theta)\right\}\right],\mathcal N\{0,W(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0,\] and the direct composite estimator \(\widehat W_n\) in the corrected \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\) is uniformly consistent for \(W(\theta)\). Gaussian-maximum calibration with \(\widehat W_n\) yields \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\left\{\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\in I_{ij,n}\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\right\}\geq1-\alpha,\] and consequently \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{G(A)\in\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\}\geq1-\alpha.\]
statements.justification: Conservative simultaneous sign inversion makes uncertainty about every directed edge visible without treating fixed-level exclusions as a support-consistent selector.
statements.gap: WangXieCuozzoMakXie2020 Section 2, Equations (2)--(5), and Theorem 3.2, Equations (7)--(8), use exact event-time likelihood scores and continuous-time martingale concentration; WangKolarShojaie2025 likewise uses exact histories. Neither provides simultaneous graph inclusion for a fixed-bin covariance inverse with unknown image rank.
statements.consumer: Alarm-network analysts can report which edges are compelled, excluded, or unresolved at a common familywise confidence level.

statements.statement: Using \(H_{\mathrm{one}}\), fix \(p=3\) and determine the injectivity locus of \(\mathcal O_1\) separately on every labeled chain, fork, and diamond support \(G_0\in\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\): for which \(\theta\in\Theta_{s,G_0}\) is \(\mathfrak F_1\{\mathcal O_1(\theta)\}\cap\Theta_{s,G_0}=\{\theta\}\)? For every \(s\in\{1,2,3\}\) and \(G_0\in\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\), determine whether there is a nonempty relatively open \(U=V\cap\Theta_{s,G_0}\), with \(V\) open under \(\rho_{\Theta}\), such that each \(\theta\in U\) admits \(\theta'\in\{\mathfrak F_1\{\mathcal O_1(\theta)\}\cap\Theta_{s,G_0}\}\setminus\{\theta\}\) with \(\rho_{\mathrm{law}}(P_{\theta},P_{\theta'})>0\).
statements.justification: The exact two-lag inverse does not itself decide whether one positive covariance lag is sufficient, so the smaller observable must be analyzed as an unresolved compatibility fiber.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 Section II-B, Theorem 1 and Equation (19), with Corollary 1, identifies from the complete covariance-density function; Kirchner2016 Section 3.3, Equations (25)--(28), and Section 4, Equation (29), gives an INAR lag route and a small-bin approximation; CheyssonLang2022 Corollary 3 gives the full aliased binned spectrum, while Theorems 2--3 assume full-spectral injectivity in condition (A2). None establishes injectivity or noninjectivity of \(m,\Gamma_1\) on the named legal three-node support strata.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether archives for three-node chain, fork, and diamond alarm motifs must retain a second positive covariance lag.

statements.statement: Using \(H_{\mathrm{boundary}}\), fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), \(\alpha\), \(\kappa_0\), and a bandwidth sequence satisfying \(b_n\to\infty\) and \(b_n=o(n^{1/2})\). Construct a data-only \(\mathfrak U_n=(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal T_n)\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)\) uniformly over the same nuisance-regular closure \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), and characterize the sharp frontier \(\mathfrak R_{n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n)=(R_{G,n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n),R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(\delta_n))\) for every sequence \(\delta_n\downarrow0\). Determine whether one honest procedure simultaneously attains both risks up to universal constants over every \(\mathcal M_{\kappa_0}(\delta_n)\), and quantify its excess graph-inclusion loss \(\ell_{\mathrm{inc}}\) relative to \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) and its excess \(\rho_{\Theta}\)-diameter relative to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\).
statements.justification: The empty graph destroys decay identification and weak singular values destroy rank selection, so honest adaptation is the substantive unresolved inference boundary.
statements.gap: WangXieCuozzoMakXie2020 Section 2 and Theorem 3.2 constructs exact-event-time likelihood-score confidence polyhedra, while CheyssonLang2022 Theorems 2--3 impose conditions (A1)--(A4), including full-spectral identifiability (A2), for fixed-model Whittle limits. Neither covers rank, edge, or empty-network approach inside one nuisance-regular closure. GleserHwang1987 Section 2, Theorem 1, supplies the general warning that a nuisance limit erasing an unbounded target forces infinite confidence sets with positive probability, but whether and at what rate that mechanism governs this bounded-metric Hawkes frontier is unresolved.
statements.consumer: The result would tell cellular-network operators when a wide graph set is statistically unavoidable rather than evidence of a failed algorithm.

statements.statement: If \(T=e^{\Delta B}\) and \(\operatorname{spec}(\Delta B)\subset\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi\}\), then \(T\) has no eigenvalue on the closed negative real axis, its principal matrix logarithm exists, and \(\operatorname{Log}(T)=\Delta B\).

source.locator: Section 2, principal logarithm and the open strip characterization
source.verbatim_statement: log(exp(A)) = A holds if and only if |Im(λi)| < π for every eigenvalue λi of A

attestation.note: Verified directly against the University of Manchester author-repository PDF, Computing Matrix Functions, p. 165, immediately after Theorem 2.6; downloaded 2026-09-05 from the persisted primary URL. Theorem 2.6 defines log as the principal logarithm and gives its unique open-strip characterization.

statements.justification: The classical principal-logarithm strip theorem is the only non-novel ingredient needed to remove matrix-exponential aliasing in the feedback branch.
statements.gap: This is classical matrix-function theory rather than a contribution of the note.
statements.consumer: The full-rank stable recovery theorem uses it to identify the continuous-time generator from the one-bin transition.

statements.statement: For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\), \(B\) is a real Hurwitz matrix, \(Q\succ0\), \(C_{+}(t)=e^{Bt}K\) for \(t>0\), \(K=A(2\beta I_p-A)Q\), \(K-K^{\mathsf T}=AD-DA^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\Gamma_k=T^{k-1}J^2K\) for every \(k\geq1\). Moreover, \(J\) is invertible, \(\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(K)=\operatorname{im}(A)\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\).
statements.justification: The stable identity is the common algebraic substrate for both the acyclic singular-rank inverse and the full-rank feedback extension.
statements.gap: Published complete-covariance and full-spectrum results do not state this exact fixed-bin semigroup and image equality for a stable common-exponential matrix.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the full-space transition and Lyapunov objects used by the full-rank inverse.

statements.statement:
Let \(\theta_a=(\beta_a,0,\mu_0)\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), be two parameters in \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\) with a common strictly positive baseline and \(\beta_0\neq\beta_1\). Then \(P_{\theta_0}=P_{\theta_1}=:P_0\), and every \(\mathfrak U_n=(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal T_n)\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)\) satisfies
\[
 P_0\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)\geq1\wedge|\beta_0-\beta_1|\right\}\geq(1-2\alpha)_+.
\]
If \(|\beta_0-\beta_1|\geq1\), then the event in the display is \(\{\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)=1\}\).
statements.justification: The proposition isolates the exact nonvanishing confidence-diameter obstruction caused by decay nonidentification at the empty graph.
statements.gap: The general Gleser--Hwang phenomenon does not itself give this bounded-metric two-decay witness for the Hawkes closure.
statements.consumer: It prevents an honest boundary procedure from reporting a spuriously narrow decay set at an empty network.

statements.statement:
Fix \(n\geq3\). Let \(\theta_s=(\beta_s,0,\mu_0)\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), have a common strictly positive baseline \(\mu_0\), distinct decays \(\beta_0\neq\beta_1\), and satisfy \(P_{\theta_s}\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\). Put \(d_{01}=1\wedge|\beta_1-\beta_0|\). Then \(P_{\theta_0}=P_{\theta_1}=:P_0\), and every \(\mathfrak U_n=(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal T_n)\in\mathfrak H_{n,\kappa_0}(\alpha)\) satisfies
\[
 P_0\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)\geq d_{01}\right\}\geq(1-2\alpha)_+.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 R_{\Theta,n,\kappa_0}(0)\geq d_{01}(1-2\alpha)_+.
\]

For \(p=3\), every labeled fork support has \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)=1\), whereas every labeled directed-chain support and every labeled three-node diamond support, meaning the transitive triangle in \(\mathfrak G_3^{\mathrm{cfd}}\), has rank two; consequently all other rank-support strata are empty. Fix a fork and relabel it as \(1\to2\) and \(1\to3\), with \(A_{21}=a>0\) and \(A_{31}=b>0\). Put \(x=a/\beta\), \(y=b/\beta\), and \(h(\beta)=(1-e^{-\beta\Delta})^2/\beta\). On this fork stratum, \((m,\Gamma_1)\) identifies \(x\), \(y\), and \(h(\beta)\). The function \(h\) has a unique maximizer \(\beta_\star=z_\star/\Delta\), where \(z_\star>0\) is the unique positive solution of \(e^{z_\star}=1+2z_\star\). The within-support one-lag fiber is a singleton exactly when \(\beta=\beta_\star\), and otherwise consists of exactly two parameter points, one on each side of \(\beta_\star\). The two points induce different laws because their second positive covariance lags differ. Thus each of \(\{\theta\in\Theta_{1,G_0}:\beta<\beta_\star\}\) and \(\{\theta\in\Theta_{1,G_0}:\beta>\beta_\star\}\) is a nonempty relatively open one-lag alias region for every labeled fork \(G_0\).
statements.justification: This is the exact computable side of the one-lag information-order question and supplies an explicit generic alias witness.
statements.gap: Existing Hawkes identification results do not classify a fixed-support fiber from only the mean and first positive covariance lag.
statements.consumer: A three-label fork archive needs a second positive lag except at the unique scalar maximizer.

statements.statement:
For every \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\), all quantities in \(\text{def:full-rank-two-lag-inverse}\) are well defined and independent of the structural representative in \(\text{def:full-rank-stable-moment-image}\). In particular, \(\Gamma_1\), \(B^\dagger\), \(J^\dagger\), \(K^\dagger\), and \(Q^\dagger\) are invertible, \(B^\dagger\) is real Hurwitz, \(Q^\dagger\succ0\) is the unique solution of \(B^\dagger Q+Q(B^\dagger)^{\mathsf T}=-D^\dagger\), and \(s^\dagger>0\). For every structural representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\),
\[
 T^\dagger=T,\quad B^\dagger=B,\quad J^\dagger=J,\quad K^\dagger=K,\quad Q^\dagger=Q,\quad s^\dagger=\beta^2,
\]
and \(\Phi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{\Delta,p}(\eta)=(\beta,A,\mu)\). Thus the mean and two positive covariance lags identify stable full-rank cyclic, reciprocal, and self-exciting common-exponential networks on the stated principal-log no-alias strip.
statements.justification: The theorem extends exact two-lag recovery to stable feedback networks while keeping the original all-bin-width singular DAG theorem intact.
statements.gap: Broad cyclic Hawkes identification uses complete lag or spectral information; it does not furnish this domain-restricted mean-plus-two-lag inverse.
statements.consumer: Full-rank alarm networks with reciprocal or self-exciting channels can be de-aliased when their generator lies in the principal-log strip.

statements.statement:
For every \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\), every quantity in \(\text{def:restricted-rank-two-lag-inverse}\) is well defined, independent of the orthonormal basis \(O\), and independent of the admissible structural representative.  More precisely, \(r\geq1\), \(R\) has full row rank, the principal logarithm of \(F\) exists, \(D^\sharp\succ0\), \(W^\sharp\succ0\), and \(L^\sharp\) and \(F-I_r\) are invertible.  For every admissible representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\), \(F\) is the coordinate matrix of \(T|_S\), \(L^\sharp\) is the coordinate matrix of \(B|_S\), \(\beta^\sharp=\beta\), \(A_S^\sharp=O^{\mathsf T}AO\), \(K^\sharp=K\), \(\mathsf C^\sharp=AD\), and
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}(\eta)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Consequently the mean and two positive covariance lags identify every amplitude, baseline, decay, and labeled edge for every nonempty stable zero-diagonal common-exponential model satisfying the principal-log strip only on \(S=\operatorname{im}(A)=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\), including singular directed cycles and reciprocal pairs.  These cases are genuine: for every \(\Delta>0\), taking \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=(1,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \(\varepsilon_\Delta=\min\{1/2,\pi/(2\sqrt3\Delta)\}\), and
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&0&\varepsilon_\Delta&0\\
 \varepsilon_\Delta&0&0&0\\
 0&\varepsilon_\Delta&0&0\\
 0&0&0&0
 \end{pmatrix}
\]
gives a stable rank-three directed cycle with an isolated label in dimension four, while taking \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/2&0\\1/2&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
gives a stable rank-two reciprocal pair with an isolated label in dimension three; both satisfy the stated restricted strip and belong to the image domain.
statements.justification: The theorem extends exact fixed-bin recovery to positive-rank singular feedback networks without replacing either the all-bin-width acyclic theorem or the ambient full-rank theorem.
statements.gap: Full-lag and full-spectrum Hawkes identification do not furnish this basis-invariant mean-plus-two-lag inverse on a singular stable-feedback image.
statements.consumer: Low-resolution alarm networks with singular directed cycles or reciprocal pairs can be de-aliased when the generator satisfies the restricted principal-log strip.

statements.statement:
For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\), and hence for every law in \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG}}\),
\[
 \Gamma_0=\Delta D+\int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{C_{+}(t)+C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt,
 \qquad m=\Delta\lambda.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 D=\Delta^{-1}\!\left[\Gamma_0-
 \int_0^\Delta(\Delta-t)
 \{C_{+}(t)+C_{+}(t)^{\mathsf T}\}\,dt\right],
 \qquad \operatorname{diag}(D)=\lambda\in(0,\infty)^p.
\]
statements.justification: The diagonal atom of the zero-lag covariance measure is the common bridge that reconstructs stationary intensity from three bin-covariance matrices.
statements.gap: The positive-lag semigroup alone does not account for the diagonal counting-measure atom inside a single bin.
statements.consumer: All three covariance-only population inverses use this identity to reconstruct the omitted mean.

statements.statement:
For every \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:full-rank-covariance-only-inverse}\) is well defined and independent of the admissible structural representative.  For every such representative,
\[
 T^0=T,\quad B^0=B,\quad J^0=J,\quad K^0=K,
 \quad \widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{fr}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\ (0<t\leq\Delta),
 \quad D^0=D,\quad m^0=m,
\]
and
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr},0}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 = (\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus three covariance matrices identify the stable full-rank principal-strip branch without a supplied mean.  The domain is strictly non-DAG: for every \(p\geq2\) and \(\Delta>0\), it contains the stationary law with \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=\mathbf 1_p\), and \(A=\tfrac12 I_p\), whose graph has a self-loop at every label.
statements.justification: It shows that zero-lag covariance replaces the mean in the ambient full-rank feedback inverse and proves a strict self-exciting non-DAG witness.
statements.gap: Complete-lag and spectral Hawkes results do not isolate this exact three-covariance fixed-bin inverse on the full-rank principal-strip image.
statements.consumer: Population covariance archives can identify full-rank reciprocal, cyclic, or self-exciting stable networks without retained marginal means.

statements.statement:
For every \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in
\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:restricted-rank-covariance-only-inverse}\) is well defined, the reconstructed curve and output are independent of the orthonormal basis \(O\), and all quantities are independent of the admissible structural representative.  For every such representative,
\[
 \widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{rs}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\ (0<t\leq\Delta),
 \qquad D^0=D,\qquad m^0=m,
\]
and
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs},0}
 (\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus three covariance matrices identify the nonempty stable zero-diagonal restricted-strip branch without a supplied mean.  For every \(\Delta>0\), this covariance image contains both a rank-three directed cycle with an isolated fourth label and a rank-two reciprocal pair with an isolated third label, so it is strictly larger than the acyclic regime.
statements.justification: It establishes a basis-invariant covariance-only inverse on the singular zero-diagonal feedback image and certifies strict cycle and reciprocal witnesses.
statements.gap: Existing second-order Hawkes identification does not provide this exact restricted-image three-covariance de-aliasing map for singular feedback networks.
statements.consumer: Covariance-only alarm summaries can recover singular cyclic or reciprocal stable networks when the restricted principal-log condition holds.

statements.statement:
For every \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:isolated-invertible-block-two-lag-inverse}\) is well defined.  If \((\beta,A,\mu,I,E_I,A_I)\) is any structural representative in \(\text{def:isolated-invertible-block-stable-moment-image}\), then
\[
 S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)=\operatorname{im}(A)
   =\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in I\},\qquad
 I=\{i:e_i\in S\},\qquad r=|I|=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),
\]
so the active label set and its ordered selector are unique.  Writing
\[
 L_I=A_I-\beta I_r,\quad
 J_I=\int_0^\Delta e^{L_Iu}\,du,\quad
 D_I=E_I^{\mathsf T}DE_I,\quad
 Q_I=\int_0^\infty e^{L_Iu}D_Ie^{L_I^{\mathsf T}u}\,du,\quad
 K_I=A_I(2\beta I_r-A_I)Q_I,
\]
the recovered quantities satisfy
\[
 F^\circ=e^{L_I\Delta},\quad L^\circ=L_I,\quad J^\circ=J_I,\quad
 K^\circ=K_I=(\beta^2I_r-L_I^2)Q_I,\quad Q^\circ=Q_I\succ0,\quad s^\circ=\beta^2>0,
\]
and
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
The output is unchanged if the active space is represented by any orthonormal basis rather than the canonical ordered selector, and it is independent of the admissible structural representative.  For every \(\Delta>0\), the domain contains the law with \(p=2\), \(\beta=1\), \(A=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,0)\), and \(\mu=\mathbf 1_2\), and it also contains the law with \(p=3\), \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=\mathbf 1_3\), and
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}1/4&1/4&0\\1/4&1/2&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus this singular branch includes self-excitation and, in the second witness, an invertible reciprocal self-exciting active block, while retaining an isolated observed label.
statements.justification: This theorem adds an exact singular-feedback branch in which the active image is a proper coordinate subspace and the active excitation block is invertible, allowing self-loops and reciprocal excitation while identifying the active labels themselves.
statements.gap: The acyclic theorem handles arbitrary singular feed-forward matrices, the zero-diagonal restricted theorem handles singular feedback without self-loops, and the full-rank theorem handles self-loops without isolated labels; none of those statements covers an invertible self-exciting active block embedded among isolated observed labels.
statements.consumer: A cellular-alarm panel may contain an interacting reciprocal subsystem together with observed alarm labels that have positive exogenous rates but no excitation links.

statements.statement:
For every \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:isolated-invertible-block-covariance-only-inverse}\) is well defined, the active label set is uniquely determined by \(S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1)\), and the recovered curve and output are independent of active-space coordinates and of the admissible structural representative.  For every such representative,
\[
 \widetilde C_{+}^{\mathrm{ib}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\quad(0<t\leq\Delta),\qquad
 D^0=D,\qquad \lambda^0=\lambda,\qquad m^0=m,
\]
and
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib},0}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Consequently three covariance matrices identify the isolated invertible-block principal-strip branch without a supplied mean.  Its covariance image contains the covariance triples of both strict witnesses in \(\text{thm:isolated-invertible-block-two-lag-recovery}\).
statements.justification: The zero-lag covariance atom recovers all innovation intensities, including those of labels isolated from excitation, and makes the proper-subset active-block inverse mean-free.
statements.gap: Existing covariance-only branches do not cover a singular ambient excitation matrix whose proper active block is invertible and may contain both reciprocal edges and self-loops.
statements.consumer: Covariance archives of coarse cellular alarms can recover an interacting active subsystem and the baselines of isolated labels even when marginal count means were not retained.

statements.statement:
Let \(N\) be a stationary \(p\)-dimensional linear Hawkes process with positive causal kernel matrix \(\phi\), suppose every entry of \(\phi\) is in \(L^1(\mathbb R_+)\), and suppose the spectral radius of the matrix \((\int_0^\infty\phi^{ij}(t)\,dt)_{i,j}\) is strictly less than one.  Define its nonsingular conditional-response density by
\[
 g^{ij}(t)\,dt
 =\mathbb E\{dN_i(t)\mid dN_j(0)=1\}
  -\mathbf 1_{\{i=j\}}\delta_0(dt)-\lambda_i\,dt.
\]
Then \(\phi\) is the unique matrix function \(\chi\) whose entries are causal and in \(L^1(\mathbb R_+)\) and which solves
\[
 g(t)=\chi(t)+(\chi*g)(t),\qquad t>0,
\]
where \((\chi*g)(t)=\int_0^\infty\chi(s)g(t-s)\,ds\) with matrix multiplication.

statements.justification: This is the published uniqueness theorem that converts the reconstructed complete conditional response into the Hawkes kernel.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 assumes the complete response is available and does not reconstruct it from two fixed-bin covariance lags.
statements.consumer: The broad stable nonzero recovery theorem uses precisely this uniqueness step after completing the response from the two observed lags.

statements.statement:
For every law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\), the nonsingular conditional-response density in \(\text{lem:bacry-muzy-wiener-hopf-uniqueness}\) agrees almost everywhere with \(g\) in \(\text{def:complete-hawkes-response}\).  Explicitly,
\[
 C_{+}(t)_{ij}=g^{ij}(t)\lambda_j\quad(t>0),
\]
and consequently
\[
 g(t)=C_{+}(t)D^{-1}\quad(t>0),\qquad
 g(t)=C_{+}(-t)^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}\quad(t<0).
\]
statements.justification: It audits the transpose and right-normalization needed to apply the published Wiener--Hopf theorem in this note's future-row covariance convention.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 writes the covariance with the earlier coordinate in the row, whereas this note writes the future coordinate in the row.
statements.consumer: The broad recovery theorem uses this bridge to pass its reconstructed covariance density to the cited conditional-response uniqueness theorem.

statements.statement:
For every \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:wiener-hopf-two-lag-inverse}\) is well defined, independent of the orthonormal basis \(O\), and independent of the admissible structural representative.  For every such representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\),
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\geq1,\quad S=\operatorname{im}(A),\quad
 F=[T|_S]_O,\quad L^{\mathrm{WH}}=[B|_S]_O,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=[J|_S]_O^{-1},
\]
\[
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=K,\quad C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\quad(t>0),\quad
 D^{\mathrm{WH}}=D,\quad g^{\mathrm{WH}}=g,\quad
 \chi^{\mathrm{WH}}=\phi,
\]
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=A/\beta,\quad M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=A/\beta^2,\quad
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}>0,\quad u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}>0,
\]
and
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus the mean and two positive fixed-bin covariance lags identify the entire stable nonzero common-exponential Hawkes mechanism, and hence its labeled graph, whenever the principal-log strip holds only on \(S=\operatorname{im}(A)\); no full-rank, zero-diagonal, coordinate-support, isolated-label, acyclicity, or invertible-active-block condition is required.  The regime is strictly broader than each such algebraic special case: for \(p=2\), every \(\Delta>0\), \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=\mathbf 1_2\), and \(A=\tfrac14\mathbf 1_2\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}\) define an admissible member whose \(A\) is singular, self-exciting, reciprocal, and has the non-coordinate image \(\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1_2)\).
statements.justification: It gives the broad population inverse requested by the directive, including singular, reciprocal, cyclic, and self-exciting stable mechanisms.
statements.gap: BacryMuzy2016 identifies the kernel from the complete conditional response, whereas this theorem first reconstructs that entire response exactly from the mean and only two fixed-bin covariance lags.
statements.consumer: Coarsely timestamped multichannel alarm systems can be structurally identified beyond feed-forward graphs when the restricted principal-log strip is scientifically credible.

statements.statement:
For every \(\gamma=(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:wiener-hopf-covariance-only-inverse}\) is well defined, independent of the orthonormal basis and of the admissible structural representative, and reconstructs
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A),\quad S=\operatorname{im}(A),\quad
 F=[T|_S]_O,\quad L^{\mathrm{WH}}=[B|_S]_O,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=[J|_S]_O^{-1},\quad K^{\mathrm{WH}}=K,
\]
\[
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\quad(t>0),\quad
 D^{\mathrm{WH},0}=D,\quad
 m^{\mathrm{WH},0}=m.
\]
For every admissible representative,
\[
 \Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH},0}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 =(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus \(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\) alone identify the same stable nonzero restricted-strip regime.
statements.justification: It removes the supplied mean by recovering the innovation-intensity matrix from the zero-lag covariance identity.
statements.gap: Complete-covariance identification does not isolate the exact three-covariance fixed-bin inverse on this broad singular stable regime.
statements.consumer: Archived alarm covariance summaries remain identifying even when marginal count means were not retained.

sampling_model.design: One stationary labeled multivariate Hawkes trajectory observed only through consecutive bins of known width \(\Delta\).
sampling_model.units: The dependent observations are \(X_0,\ldots,X_{n-1}\); the population identification result precedes sampling asymptotics.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the target is the directed excitation mechanism \((\beta,A,\mu)\) and its graph \(G(A)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification leverage comes from nonnegative acyclic excitation and a common exponential decay.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the raw mean and cross-moment vector \(\xi=\mathbb E[Y_0]\), apply \(\eta=\mathcal C(\xi)=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), select \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)\) by singular-value thresholding, and estimate the raw-moment long-run covariance \(\Omega(\theta)\) by a lag-window estimator. The single composite Jacobian \(\mathcal J(\theta)=D(\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\) produces both \(V(\theta)\) and the signed-edge covariance \(W(\theta)\). Uniform geometric mixing and the eighth-bin-count envelope are derived from finite-depth Poisson branching on the bounded fixed-margin class; the remaining inference restrictions are long-run covariance nonsingularity and the stated bandwidth condition. Support selection uses the separate vanishing threshold \(a_n\), while fixed-level Gaussian-maximum inversion is used only for conservative simultaneous-coordinate and graph-inclusion coverage.

estimand_functional: On \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), \((\beta,A,\mu)=\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\), and on \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), \((\beta,A,\mu)=\Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH},0}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\). These broad images contain every nonzero law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{stab}}\) whose restricted generator \(\Delta(A-\beta I_p)|_{\operatorname{im}(A)}\) lies in the principal-log strip. The four explicit algebraic branches remain: on \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), \((\beta,A,\mu)=\Phi_{\Delta,r}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=\Psi_{\Delta,r}(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\) with \(r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1)\); on \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\) and \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\), the corresponding maps are \(\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs}}\) and \(\Psi_{\Delta,p}^{0,+,\mathrm{rs},0}\); on \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\) and \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\), they are \(\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr}}\) and \(\Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{fr},0}\); and on \(\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\) and \(\mathfrak J_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\), they are \(\Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib}}\) and \(\Psi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{ib},0}\).

tldr: Coarse timestamping need not erase Hawkes direction when a labeled feed-forward network is acyclic and all edges share one unknown exponential decay. Acyclicity is the contribution-defining scientific restriction: self-loops are allowed by the graph convention and therefore excluded as cycles of length one, rather than by a separate zero-diagonal assumption. The core claim is that the stationary mean and exactly two positive fixed-bin covariance matrices determine the active image \(\operatorname{im}(A)\), the decay through the restricted transition, the finite nilpotent logarithm, every directed amplitude through an antisymmetric covariance jump, and the baselines. Koyama2025 gives a third-order small-bin spectral approximation for a coarse-grained process, and Kirchner2016 gives an INAR(\(\infty\)) approximation as the mesh vanishes; the inverse here is exact at every fixed known \(\Delta>0\) for the original process and remains valid for singular excitation matrices, repeated poles, disconnected components, diamonds, and proportional rows. The empty graph is exactly the \(\beta\)-nonidentified stratum. A covariance-only corollary and a bounded-Lipschitz uniform Gaussian theorem use the single composite Jacobian \(D(\Phi_{\Delta,r}\circ\mathcal C)\). The thresholded graph \(\widehat G_n\), with vanishing thresholds slower than \(n^{-1/2}\), is support consistent; fixed-level sign inversion instead gives conservative simultaneous-coordinate and graph-inclusion coverage with asymptotic lower bound \(1-\alpha\), not exact coverage or support recovery. One-lag injectivity on named three-node motifs and honest adaptation over a nuisance-regular closure remain open.

honest_scope: The exact inverse is claimed only for stationary labeled linear Hawkes laws with known fixed \(\Delta\), positive baselines, nonnegative excitation, the contribution-defining feed-forward acyclicity restriction, one common exponential decay, and at least one edge. The graph convention admits self-loops before acyclicity is imposed, so acyclicity implies both \(A_{ii}=0\) and stability because \(A\) is nilpotent; neither zero diagonal nor stability is imposed separately. In the two-node one-edge special case, \(F=e^{-\beta\Delta}\) and the sign of \(K-K^{\mathsf T}\) recovers the familiar unique direction. At \(A=0\), the model reduces to independent Poisson counts and \(\beta\) is left unidentified. The bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian approximation and HAC consistency are claimed only on \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\). The fixed-level graph set has only the conservative guarantees \(\liminf_n\inf_{\theta}P_{\theta}\{\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\in I_{ij,n}\text{ for all }i<j\}\geq1-\alpha\) and \(\liminf_n\inf_{\theta}P_{\theta}\{G(A)\in\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\}\geq1-\alpha\); equality with \(1-\alpha\) is not claimed, and its fixed-level sign decisions are not a support-recovery result. Uniform support recovery belongs only to the separately thresholded \(\widehat G_n\), with \(t_n,a_n\downarrow0\) and \(\sqrt n\,t_n,\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\). Uniform geometric mixing and the eighth-bin-count bound are derived conclusions. Boundary honesty remains open over the single nuisance-regular closure \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\), which keeps decay, parameter, intensity, variance, derived mixing, derived moment, and HAC bandwidth conditions regular while allowing rank, edges, and \(A=0\) to approach the boundary. One-lag injectivity or noninjectivity is not established; the open question is restricted to labeled three-node chain, fork, and diamond supports. Heterogeneous decays, feedback cycles, hidden labels, and growing \(p\) also remain unresolved.
